They take two byes. Bangladesh creating chances here.
Bangs in a short ball on middle and leg, Kusal sits under it. A maiden!
Driven straight to the man at cover.
Now Rahman is seen flirting with the danger zone in his followthrough. Needs to be careful here as umpire Rod Tucker has been really strict all this while.
Angling away outside off, another leave from Mendis.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, KM lets it be.
On a good length and just outside off, defended off the back foot.
Silva flicks it towards the man at mid-wicket for nothing.
Flattish outside off, punched to sweeper cover for a single.
Quicker ball on the stumps, worked away towards mid-wicket for a single.
Gets behind the line and blocks.
Turning back in from a length outside off, flicked through backward square leg for a single.
Spinning down leg, Mendis goes back to flick but fails to work it away. A good take from Das.
Goes fuller, a bit on off, worked away towards mid on.
One Silva replaces another. Roshen Silva walks in next.

OUT! Top edge and it's taken! A wicket against the run of play, the second new ball doing the trick, a rash approach. You call it what you want. To be honest, de Silva who was fluent all throughout his innings, looked a bit overconfident after the lunch break. Rahman drops it on a length and angles it away outside off. Dhananjaya stands tall and looks to pull it away but gets hurried on due to the zip extracted by the new ball. Gets a healthy top edge that skies straight up in the air. Liton Das calls for it, runs in front towards point and takes it. Even Rahman goes for it but seeing the keeper charging in, he aborts. Finally, finally Bangladesh have struck and have put an end to a marathon partnership of 308 runs. Sri Lanka still trail by 205 runs.
Sprays it on a fuller length, wider outside off, the batsman shoulders his arms.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Stands back to this length ball and defends it down.

Fuller and wider outside off, de Silva looks to jam this one out but it goes to the keeper. A stifled appeal for a caught behind but the sound was of the bat hitting the ground and hence the umpire shakes his head.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A bit short and flatter through the air, Mendis taps it in front of point. Wants a single but won't get it.
Mendis bunts it back to the bowler.
Fractionally short and bowled outside off, Mendis punches it through sweeper cover for a brace.
Flatter one outside off, knocked down to long on for one.

Was that a catch? Oh, yes indeed! Full marks to Liton Das for his efforts! He is quick to see what Dhananjaya was shaping up for. De Silva walks across the sticks, Mehidy serves it down the leg side. The right-hander goes for the paddle but ends up getting it off the splice. Das dives to his left, gets a glove to it but fails to hold on. Had that been taken, my word, it would have been a stunner. Chance goes down, nevertheless.
FOUR! Creamed it! Rahman goes fuller, it turns out to be a half-volley. Mendis takes a stride forward and drives it past the man at mid off. The new ball does the rest. It races away to the fence.
Slanting away on a back of a length in the fifth stump channel, slapped towards sweeper cover for a single.
Good length delivery on middle, defended with a slightly closed face of the bat towards mid-wicket.
Angling away on a fuller length outside off, DdS makes an assured leave.

A record broken! This is the first time in this Test that runs have come in the form of leg byes. Rahman once again strays around the pads, de Silva moves inside the line to clip it away but gets it off the pads down to fine leg. Two leg byes taken, first extras in this innings. Also, triple century comes up.

The umpires are having a chat with de Silva. Not sure what was it regarding. Maybe, because the batter walked down the track and was seen on the danger area. Well, I didn't know that even when you take the charge, you aren't allowed to step on the red zone.
Interesting! He comes in from over the wicket but serves it down the leg side. Dhananjaya dances down the track and looks to clip it away but fails to get any wood on it.
The second new ball is available now. And Bangladesh have opted for it straightaway. Mustafizur Rahman to taste the new cherry first. Can he strike? Three slips in place. Good attacking move.
Hasan gives it air, lands it outside off, Kusal bunts it back to the bowler.
Flighted delivery around off, worked off the inner half as the ball rolls past the short leg fielder.
Flatter ball outside off, helped with a dab past the first slip fielder for a couple of runs towards third man.
Let's the ball dip in, Mendis works it straight to the fielder at short mid-wicket.
Lands it on off, turning back in, clipped off the back foot past short leg.
Run to start with! Tossed up ball outside off, dipping in, de Silva gets down, takes it on the full to sweep it in front of square on the leg side to get to the other end.

We are back for the post-lunch session. Will we see Bangladesh coming out with a plan and tasting success? Both the batsmen are set to resume their innings. Dhananjaya de Silva will face the first ball. Mehidy Hasan has the ball. Let's play...
... Day 3, Second Session ...

Bangladesh look down and out at the moment. They look hapless against the two batsmen out there and none of their bowlers have an answer to stop the rampage. The left-arm spinners opted for negative lines to dry the run-flow while their skipper went all defensive with his field placements. The fact that Mehidy Hasan wasn't given to bowl much, should keep you thinking. Anyway, Sri Lanka are still 218 runs adrift and if they manage to continue in the same manner, they will be ahead of the hosts at some stage later in the day. The second new ball is just one over away. Will that bring about the change in fortunes for the home side? Or will the churning game go on? Join us back for the second session in a short while...

Back-to-back wicketless sessions and no need to say who take the honours this morning. Sri Lanka continue to dominate the proceedings with both their overnight batsmen, Kusal Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva ruling the roost and making merry on this docile surface. They haven't offered any chance to the hosts and have been successful in motoring along. Both look set big time and look hungry for more. Double ton is there for the taking and they would look to get one under their belts.
Flatter delivery on the leg stump, Kusal Mendis gets it off the inner half past short leg. LUNCH, DAY 3!
Fuller on the stumps, defended nicely off the front foot and into the ground.
Shorter and wider on off, de Silva stays back and punches it towards deep cover for a single.
Around middle and leg, wristed through square leg for one.
Quicker delivery, a bit close to the off stump, Mendis shapes up for the cut shot but it's too close to do so. Chops it towards the backward point fielder.
Tossed up outside off, pushed towards the mid off fielder.
We will get one more over in before lunch.
Drifting in from around off, de Silva stabs it out.
Covers the line and blocks.
Slower delivery, turning back in from a length, worked in front of square leg for a single.
Flattish delivery on the stumps, Mendis hangs back and shows a straight blade.

FOUR! Deft! Mehidy Hasan bowls it quicker through the air, outside off, Mendis makes room and cuts it really late. Gets it past Imrul Kayes at first slip, who gives it a chase. But his tired legs mean that the ball wins the race.
Spinning back in around leg, clipped towards short fine leg for a single.
Tossed up on the stumps, driven straight to the man at cover.
De Silva pushes it through cover for a single.
Flighted outside off, defended with a lunge forward.

FOUR! Delightful stuff! Left me in awe! Excellent use of the feet and then those wrists come into play! Simply superb! Floated delivery around middle and off, Dhananjaya skips down the track and wrists it cleanly over mid-wicket to pick up a boundary.
Gets behind the line and stabs it out.
Flighted delivery on off, de Silva comes down the track, takes it on the full and pushes it back to the bowler.
Another change. Taijul Islam comes back into the attack.
This one nearly went through! Flatter one, skids off the surface and stays a bit low too. Mendis crouches low and brings his bat down at the right time to keep it out in the direction of the bowler.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Stays back, allows the ball to turn back in and then clips it through square leg for a single.
Takes a stride forward, drives but finds the man at mid off.
Slower through the air but the length is a tad short, defended off the back foot.
Flighted delivery outside off, de Silva straightaway dances down the track and drives it towards mid off where Mominul Haque makes a tumbling stop.
Here he comes. The only one to pick up a wicket, Mehidy Hasan is FINALLY brought into the attack. Can he provide the breakthrough? The second new ball is 30 balls away.
Hangs back and works it towards the man at square leg.
Drops it short around leg, worked away through square leg for a single.
Shamim Chowdhury makes a point on air. He feels that going in with just one pacer isn't the best idea. Variation in pace plays a big role, especially when the wickets are hard to come by.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Flatter one outside off, punched to long on for one.

FOUR! Pulled away! Drops it short and down the leg side, Mendis sinks low and pulls it over square leg. The man in the deep gets to the ball, gets a hand to it but fails to stop it from crossing the fence.
Drifting in from outside off, slapped towards deep point for a single.
Mahmudullah brings himself on. Another throw of the dice.
Flighted delivery around off, makes a bit of room and pushes it down to long off for a single.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Tossed up outside off, driven towards long off for a single.
Loopy delivery outside off, driven towards the cover fielder.
Another short ball on middle, punched past the man at mid-wicket for a single.
Drops it short and served outside off, cut through point for a single.
Milked down to long off for an easy single.
Another couple! Quicker and flatter one outside off, Dhananjaya makes room and guides it past the lone slip fielder to collect a brace.

On the shorter length around leg, clipped through square leg and this time the batsmen come back for two. 1000 Test runs for de Silva in just 23 innings! Becomes the joint-fastest for Sri Lanka along with Roy Dias and Michael Vandort.
Slower through the air outside off, punched through cover for a single.
Flattish delivery around middle and leg, punched past the man at short mid-wicket to pick up a single.
Slides it in from around the wicket, Kusal with a lean forward drives it through cover for a single.
Tossed up around middle and leg, Dhananjaya presses forward to keep it out.
Gets right behind the line and blocks it out.
Flatter one outside off, Kusal doesn't play at it.
Loopy delivery outside off, eased down to long off for a single.
Flighted delivery around middle and leg, clipped towards mid-wicket.
That's why! Turn on the very first ball! Mendis wears a smile on his face! He pitches it around off and gets it to turn away appreciably, Mendis makes an easy leave.
More left-arm spin! Mominul Haque is brought into the attack. Hard to fathom why Bangladesh is not bringing Mehidy Hasan on.
Around middle and leg, worked down to long on for a single.
De Silva is happy to milk a single by nudging it towards square leg.
Flatter delivery on leg, defended back to the bowler off the back foot.
Floated outside leg, whipped away to deep square leg for a single.
Lands it outside leg, defended with a lunge forward.
Fuller around middle and leg, Mendis blocks it back to the bowler.
Mehidy Hasan is having a long chat with Mahmudullah.
Drops it a bit short around leg, clipped through square leg to keep strike.
Outside leg, turning in towards off, Mendis stays back to keep it out.

150 up for Dhananjaya de Silva! He continues to amaze us! Beautiful knock. A bit shorter around middle and off, punched down to long off for a single. Just a raise of the bat from him. Now, can he get to a double ton?
A bit too full on the leg stump, driven down to long on to bring de Silva back on strike.
Flatter through the air around leg, tucked through square leg for an easy single. Moves to 149!
Flatter delivery around middle and leg, punched back down the track.
Loopy outside off, Kusal Mendis lunges forward in defense.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
De Silva dances down the track but yorks himself. What does he do? Jams it down to long off for a single.
Lands it on middle and leg, blocked.
Flighted delivery around middle and leg, worked wide of mid on for a single.
A bit too full, pitched around middle and off, blocked into the ground.
Pitching outside leg, turning in, safely defended back down.
Darted on the leg stump, nudged away in front of square leg for a single.
Takes a stride forward and kills it into the turf.
Dipping in on middle and leg, worked away through square leg to bring up the 250 for Sri Lanka. These two are going strong and it doesn't seem like they will stop.
Very full around middle and leg, de Silva jams it out.
A bit fuller, pitched around leg, de Silva hides his bat behind the pads to kick it away.
Slower through the air, dipping in on leg, Mendis defends it back down the track.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Slower through the air, but on the shorter length, clipped through square leg for a single.
Shimmies down the track and bunts it back down the track.
Drifting in on middle and leg, pushed back to Sunzamul.
Floated delivery around middle and leg, blocked again.
Maiden! Very full on the stumps, KM blocks.
Flatter delivery around middle and off, defended off the back foot.
Floated ball around middle and leg, Mendis stonewalls it.
Quicker through the air, but a bit too full, clipped through the leg side.
Leans forward a touch and nudges it towards the man at mid-wicket.
Tosses it up from over the wicket, Kusal presses forward in defense.
Floated ball on the stumps, de Silva takes a stride forward and pushes it back to the bowler.
Slower through the air, but this time he drags his length back just a touch. Mendis goes back and clips it to the square leg fielder.
Around middle and leg, another solid defense on offer.
Nice loop again, Kusal is happy to press forward and keep it out.
Nice loop again, lands it around leg, defended into the ground.
Flighted delivery around leg, blocked solidly by prodding ahead.
Defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Served around leg, de Silva pads this one as well.
Athar Ali Khan is questioning the logic of not going to Mehidy Hasan in the first hour. Clearly, the leader of your spin attack should have been given a role soon.
Around leg, padded away.
DdS gets behind the line of the ball and blocks it out.
Similar ball, Dhananjaya goes back and pushes it with soft hands through backward square leg. Has enough time to come back for the second.
Taijul comes over the wicket and bowls it around leg. De Silva pushes it back to the bowler off the back foot.

Time for some drinks! Sri Lanka continue to motor along well. They have taken 58 runs off the first hour, wherein 15 overs have been bowled. The pair has looked commanding, to say the least. Their mammoth 245-run stand stands testimony to that. Bangladesh haven't been incisive enough with the ball and have continued to go with the flow. Can they find a way to break this stand?
Short in length down leg, Dhananjaya pulls it through backward square leg. There is a fielder manning that area and just a single results.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Around leg, de Silva pads it away.
Islam comes over the wicket now. Bowls it around middle and leg, defended.
The cap goes out and the helmet comes in for Dhananjaya now.
FOUR! It is heartening to see the way these youngsters play spin. This ball is flighted outside off, Dhananjaya gets down on one knee and slog sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Kusal gets to the other end by driving it to long off.
Pushed to the cover region by DdS.
Good use of the feet. Dhananjaya uses his feet to get down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace.

SAFE! Floated outside off, de Silva lunges forward to defend but misses. Das whips the bails off in a flash and asks the query to the umpire, who takes it upstairs. Joel Wilson, the third umpire, is happy to make his decision on having the first look, as Dhananjaya's back foot is firmly grounded.
Have Bangladesh got the breakthrough that they want? Liton Das seems pretty confident to have stumped Dhananjaya. It is referred upstairs.
A forward defense displayed to this one in line of the stumps.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
SIX! Beautifully struck. Tossed up ball around off, de Silva slinks down the track in a flash and hits it straight as an arrow for half a dozen.
Eased through mid off for one.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.
This is driven through covers for one.

FOUR! Kusal Mendis will remember his 23rd birthday for some time now. He gets to his 4th Test century and in some style. This one is floated well outside off, Kusal uses his feet to get to the pitch of the ball and hits it over wide mid on. Raises his helmet and the bat and that's that for a celebration. He knows that a personal milestone is just a step for the larger cause, that is taking lead over the opposition. His side is still 284 runs behind.
Flatter outside off, Dhananjaya goes back to guide it to third man. Does so off the bottom edge past slip. A run taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Defended with a stride forward.
This ball is played towards covers.
Outside off, cut away to point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Punched off the back foot towards covers.

FOUR! It is a boundary, as the ball bounced just inside the ropes. This is floated on the stumps, Mendis gets down and goes across the line. Gets it over mid-wicket and the ball seems to have landed on the ropes. But further looks confirm that it landed just inside.
The umpires are checking whether this one has gone the distance or no...
This one is driven straight back. 8 runs off the over.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On 57.1, the ball fell well short of the cover fielder. The Hawk Eye is rolled in. It shows that the ball would have missed the leg stump. So, a good decision by the umpire.
FOUR! Sunzamul hasn't started well today. Bowls a half-tracker this time. De Silva goes back and pulls it over mid-wicket for another boundary.
Flatter outside off, left alone.
Outside off, driven to covers.
FOUR! Short ball, punished. This is served outside off, Dhananjaya stays back and cuts it fiercely through point for a boundary.
Sunzamul Islam to have a go with the ball now.
On the stumps, defended from the crease.
Driven towards the mid off region.
FOUR! Authoritative! Floated on the stumps, Mendis slinks down the track and lofts it over wide mid on for a boundary.
De Silva turns this towards square leg and sets off for a run. There is no hesitation from Mendis and makes it in safely before Das nails the direct hit at his end after getting to the ball quickly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

What's happening there? An appealing fair? Taijul fires it full in line of the stumps, Dhananjaya is caught on the crease as he looks to jam it out. The ball lobs off something towards covers. Before the further action is completed, the keeper and the slip yell in appeal but the bowler doesn't. Sees the ball lob towards covers, where the fielder doesn't seem to have taken it and then Islam starts appealing. None of it is upheld. Further replays show that it landed on the boot and then came off the bat, for which Liton and Kayes were appealing.
Well outside off, left alone.
Blocked firmly off the front foot.

Full in length around middle, Dhananjaya clips it through mid-wicket. Rahim, by his own admission, isn't the best of the fielders in the side. He chases it down and parries it to the man in the deep, who came there running to his left. Three runs taken in the interim.
Full on off, defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Another length ball outside off, Kusal lets it be.

Length ball outside off from round the wicket, Mendis sees it and lets it be. Mr. Chowdhury continues his rants about this angle not being effective. The Fizz came over the wicket on only the last ball of the last over.
Around off, defended towards silly point. Maiden.
Mendis gets his bat in front of his pad and defends this.
Outside off, driven to cover.
KM has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Mendis prods forward and defends.
Kusal goes back and punches it to cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, driven through covers.

FOUR! Educated edge, shouts Ricky, my colleague! On a length well outside off, de Silva stands tall and looks to guide it to third man. Gets the desired result but it ends up going off the outer half. Moves to 116 in a stand that is worth 204. Sri Lanka still trail by 309.
This ball is defended off the front foot onto the ground.

FOUR! Good ball and equally well played. Rahman angles it in on a fuller length. De Silva is awake to this one on and wrists it through mid-wicket. The timing is very good and the ball trickles away to the fence, even though it slows down. The 200-run stand between Dhananjaya and Mendis is raised. Another look showed that the batter was standing well outside the crease and that enabled him convert the length ball to a fairly full one.
Mustafizur comes round the wicket and hurls it outside off. Dhananjaya covers his stumps to let it go.
Full outside off, kept out towards covers.
In line of the stumps, Mendis gets his bat in front of the stumps and stonewalls it.
Full on off, pushed towards covers.
Defended off the front foot by KM.
Similar shot displayed to this one around off.
Around off and middle, blocked off the front foot.
Now, Rahman comes over the wicket. Angles it away from Kusal, who opens the face of the bat to guide it to third man and retain strike.

Shamim Chowdhury on air says that he would like Mustafizur Rahman to come over the wicket and use the natural angle that a left arm bowler gets. Although he isn't overly unhappy with this, he reckons that when he will bowl over the wicket, the angle will aid him more.
Hurled outside off, Mendis lets it be.
On off, defended with a stride forward.
Full outside off, Mendis lunges forward and shoulders arms.
Fuller in length on off, defended off the front foot.
Back of a length in line of the stumps, de Silva hops and pats it towards mid on and rotates strike. He is happy to take singles this morning.
Kusal negotiates the last ball by lunging forward.
Fuller this time, driven to covers.
Around off, Mendis goes back and punches it towards covers.
Tossed up around off and middle, defended off the front foot onto the ground.
De Silva drives it through mid on and gets to the other end. He crawls to 107 now.
Bowled in line of the stumps, pushed towards mid on.
Another one outside off, left alone.
Outside off, well alone.

FOUR! The birthday boy gets a slice of luck going his way! Rahman lands it on a length in the zone of apprehension. Mendis hangs his bat out at that to defend. Gets squared up a touch but ends up playing it with soft hands. The ball grabs a thick outside edge and flies right through first and second slip and races away to the fence. The ball did carry but went through the two of them. Streaky runs to move off the overnight score for Kusal.
A touch shorter in length outside off, Mendis gets a thick outside edge towards gully.
Outside off, shouldered arms to by Kusal.
Length delivery outside off, de Silva stands back and opens the face of the bat to guide it to third man for a single.
This one is driven to the man at mid off.
Another one around off, pushed towards covers.
Served around off and middle, Kusal lunges forward and blocks it down.
This is bowled outside off, defended towards covers.
Outside off, driven through mid off for one. First run for the day.
Floated on off, de Silva comes down the track and pushes it towards the bowler.
Taijul Islam to bowl from the other end.
Another one outside off, Mendis lets it be. A maiden over to start the day.
Well outside off, Kusal lets it be.

Yes, yes! That is the ideal line, that can trouble even the set batsman. Further than good length in the channel of apprehension, Mendis wafts his bat at that to defend but the ball just whizzes past the outside edge and goes to the keeper. Roshen Abeysinghe on air says that the track perhaps is playing its tricks, to which Shamim Chowdhury replies that this delivery has nothing to do with the surface.
Another one further away from the stump, Kusal minds his own business by letting it be.
This is bowled wide outside off, Mendis doesn't bother playing at that.
Runs in from round the wicket and lands it full around off. Mendis gets behind it and pushes it towards mid off.
The men who matter are out in the middle. Mustafizur Rahman will begin the day with the ball and Kusal Mendis will face him. Two slips stand in position.

Chandika Hathurusingha has a chat before the start of play and he says that he feels proud to come back and coach the national side of his country. States that Sri Lanka took their time to understand the track offered in the tri-series earlier and then adapted well in the end. Adds that they have done well in this game so far. About the transitional phase that is often talked about, he iterates that there is nothing special been done in their dressing room. Adds that it is all about common sense and assigning roles to individuals. Reckons that small things like identifying individual and their skill-sets for the job is the way forward. Cites Dushmantha Chameera being assigned to bowl with the new ball in ODIs as an example. Mentions that their first aim is to take it as close as they can and then take it session-by-session from there.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is out there inspecting the surface. The first thing he states is that the key to play on this track is to let the ball come to you as a batsman like Mendis and de Silva largely did. Observes that an area outside the right-hander's off stump is a bit rough and that could be crucial. Reckons that use of feet would be crucial as well against spin.

Moving over to Bangladesh. Life is often simple and that should be the case for their bowlers as well. Wickets - that is the one word they would be aiming for. But it is easier said than done. By virtue of them putting up over 500 when they batted, they still have 326 runs to play with. The track should aid bowling as the game nears the end. We'll reserve our comments about the pitch for the report, that we'll have shortly. Welcome to Day 3 of this first Test between Bangladesh and Sri Lanka and we'd love to have your company throughout the day's play.

A youngster is often noticed when he stands up in adverse conditions. Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis certainly feature in such a list. Remember Mendis' 176 against Australia? The current innings may not be as high in value as that one but nevertheless, it has been a vital one. He is still 17 short of his 4th ton in Tests. Now move your focus to de Silva. His previous outing was one where his entire side was hampered by unconducive weather conditions. Then, he showed character to brave a groin strain to make 119 then. Here he is, unbeaten on 104 and making sure his side is still in the game. Just to add more numbers, these two are amidst a 187-run partnership.
... Day 3, First Session ...

What does Day 3 have for us? More batting from Sri Lanka? Maybe. The track is still good enough to bat and the tourists would be expected to make use of that. Bangladesh, on the other hand, would believe that they are just a wicket or two away from making inroads. Join us tomorrow to see how the story rolls on. 0930 local time (0330 GMT) is the time. Take care, adios! Meanwhile, you can switch tabs to get a feel of some ODI cricket. South Africa and India clash in the first of their 6-match series and you would have your time's worth.

Richard Halsall, the assistant coach of Bangladesh is up for a chat. He reckons that it is still good to be in their dressing room. States that if Sri Lanka bat well tomorrow, they'll be ahead. Opines that their (own) batters have done well to post over 500. Asserts that his side stresses on having big partnerships and that's what worked for them. Concedes that the lack of spin has hampered his side. Says that he doesn't think any of their reviews was taken in desperation. Ends saying that if they have three more good sessions, they could be bossing the game.

Dhananjaya de Silva is batting post his 4th Test hundred while Kusal Mendis is keeping him company. The latter is 17 away from his triple figure score. At this point in time, it is good to remember that he has been given a couple of lives - first by Mehidy Hasan and then by Imrul Kayes. How much more will he make them pay for that? Talking about the home side's bowling, their only success came on the 15th ball of the innings and since then, it has been a barren run. Not that they haven't been disciplined enough but perhaps the track doesn't have much in it for the bowlers, although the odd ball plays the trick. A laudable point - Bangladesh haven't yet bowled an extra in this innings so far.

Test cricket at its best. A wicketless session for Sri Lanka, showing that there is nothing unusual on the track to cause discomfort to them. Initially, after Dimuth Karunaratne, who had been their mainstay in the past year, was out for a duck, it seemed as if the others will follow suit. But kudos to these youngsters to have stuck it out there. They have grinded and grafted their way to an unbeaten 187-run stand.
This is bowled around middle and leg, defended solidly by Dhananjaya to see the day off. STUMPS, DAY 2!
Last ball of the day...
Islam comes over the wicket and bowls it around leg. De Silva pads it away.
De Silva goes back and punches it towards covers.
Outside off, pushed through covers for one.
Fired down the leg side, Mendis misses the flick and it goes off the pads into the keeper's gloves. A stifled appeal made to no avail.
Mendis lunges forward and defends it with a straight bat.
Mendis retains strike with a flick through mid-wicket.
Kusal prods forward and blocks it down.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floated on the stumps, hit to mid-wicket.
In line of the stumps, pushed down to long on for one.
Mendis turns it through mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Mosaddek Hossain to roll his arm over. Last two overs left in the day's play.
Bowled on the stumps, defended off the front foot onto the ground.

FOUR! Dhananjaya de Silva gets to his fourth Test century in a pretty simple manner. Anticlimatic delivery, after having a backward short leg apart from a cover, mid off and point. This is flatter outside off, de Silva goes back and punches it through the gap between mid off and covers for a boundary. Back-to-back tons for him, his previous one being a testing one against India. No real celebrations from him as he just punches the air with his fist, before thanking the Almighty for this feat. Removes his cap and raises the bat to sink in the applause that he is getting. Top innings. At this point, Sri Lanka are still 330 runs behind.
Dhananjaya de Silva is on strike. He is on 99. The hosts are taking their time to get their field right. A backward square leg in place.
Slapped through covers for one to get his partner on strike.
Kusal gets forward and pushes it towards mid on.
Shorter in length, Mendis goes back and chips it over mid-wicket for two less than a boundary.
Very full on off and middle, squeezed out towards square leg.
Flatter outside off, slapped through cover-point for a couple. Moves to 99 now.
De Silva goes back and nudges it to mid-wicket.
Outside off, pushed to mid off.
Fuller on the stumps, driven straight back.
Bowled in line of the stumps, defended with a prod.
Flatter outside off, de Silva goes back and guides it past slip for a brace. Gets to 97 with that.
Landed outside off, driven to covers.
Defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Turned to mid-wicket for nothing.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Mendis fails to defend it with a lunge forward. Gets hit on the pads that draws a stifled appeal.
Fuller outside off, driven to the man at mid off.
Served on the stumps, Kusal goes back and defends.
De Silva keeps it out with a defense off the front foot.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Floated on the stumps, Dhananjaya gets down the track and bunts it down.
De Silva presses forward and defends this one.
Outside off, driven through covers for one.
Around off and middle, blocked.
Kusal retains strike with a drive to long off.
Outside off, Mendis looks to cut but misses.

The big smile on Mendis' face shows that the original call of NOT OUT is upheld. Floated outside off, Kusal lunges forward to defend but seems to have missed it. Liton Das takes that and puts in a huge appeal. The others join him, too. However, Marais Erasmus stays unmoved. Now, Mahmudullah challenges the same. Another look show that it is not right to have done that. Snicko doesn't show any disturbance and that means BANGLADESH LOSE BOTH THEIR REVIEWS!
Time for another review! There is a caught behind appeal against Mendis and it is taken upstairs by Bangladesh after the umpire rules it in the batter's favor.
Dhananjaya drives it through mid off for one.
Around middle, defended off the front foot onto the ground.
On middle and leg, flicked away through square leg for one.
Cut away straight to the man at backward point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
DdS slinks down the track and blocks it.
FOUR! Shot! Full outside off, drilled through covers for a boundary. Dhananjaya moves to 94 now.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.

NOT OUT! Mendis is well in. He pushes it towards mid off and sets off to the other end. There is a direct hit at the bowler's end as Kusal tries to make it in. The ball deflects towards mid on. The umpire waits for the ball to stop and refers it upstairs. The replays confirm that the batsman has made it in.
Direct hits are often interesting. There is one at the bowler's end even as Mendis tries to make it in. It is referred upstairs. This one should be good for the batter.
Sunzamul Islam back on.
De Silva defends this ball off the front foot. Another maiden for Taijul.
On the stumps, blocked.

NOT OUT! The three-meter rule saves de Silva! Floated up in line of the stumps, Dhananjaya gets down the track and looks to flick but misses. Gets rapped on the pads that draws huge appeal from the fielding side. On not getting the nod, it is taken upstairs by Mahmudullah. The first look shows that the batter is down the track more than 3 meters from the stumps and hence it is umpire's call. The review isn't lost though.
Big moment! Is that it for Dhananjaya today? An LBW appeal against him is referred upstairs by Bangladesh. Looks close.
Tossed up in line of the stumps, DdS defends but does so onto his pads off the inner half.
Dhananjaya gets forward and blocks it.
Full on off, driven through mid off for one.
Cheekier, same result. Dhananjaya gets down on one knee and paddles it aerially towards fine leg for a couple. He moves to 90 with that.
Floated around middle, de Silva gets down and paddles it down the leg side for a brace.
Punched through covers to rotate strike.
Flicked away through square leg for a single.
That stayed low! Shorter in length, de Silva goes back to punch it. Ends up chopping it back towards the bowler.
Around off and middle, defended with a forward lunge.
Bowled on the stumps, kept out with a forward defense. A maiden for Taijul.
A touch short in length, pushed towards covers.
Floated on off, Kusal presses forward and bunts it.
Mendis keeps it out with a forward defense.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
On off and middle, defended off the front foot.

Well done, Fizz! This ball is punched through covers. Seems that the ball has enough in it to go to the fence. Rahman gets to his right and does well to get down and keep the ball in play. A couple of runs result.
Outside off, driven to mid off.

Hasan comes round the wicket and tosses it up around middle and leg. Dhananjaya clips it aerially towards square leg and sets off for a run. The player from mid-wicket gets to the ball and fires a wild throw to the keeper, which beats him as well as the slip fielder, both of whom went down in tandem as they try to stop that with a dive. The ball rolls towards deep backward point and another run is taken on the overthrow.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, de Silva looks to cut but misses.
Flatter outside off, punched through covers for two.
Bowled in line of the stumps, defended.

Pitching IN LINE, impact in line and HEIGHT is the factor! Mendis survives, you can guess the decision flashed on the big screen - NOT OUT! Floated up around middle and leg, Kusal looks to block but gets beaten due to the spin on that. Gets struck on the back leg. Bangladesh appeal and on not getting the nod, decide to challenge the call. The on-field call is retained due to what Hawk Eye showed. A review lost for the hosts.
Bangladesh appeal for an LBW against Mendis and don't get the decision in their favour. They opt to take it upstairs now. Pitching could be interesting to see...
KM blocks it off the front foot.

Huge appeal from Bangladesh! Floated on the stumps, Mendis lunges forward to defend. The ball strikes him on the pads, as it seems on the first look, and the hits the bat. The players appeal to no avail. Mahmudullah asks whether to review it and gets a negative response. IT WAS BAT, NO PAD AT ALL! Good for the hosts that they didn't go upstairs.
Flicked away towards square leg for nothing.
Yorker on the stumps, dug out back towards the bowler.
DDS has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Around middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for one. Brings up the 150-run stand between these two. They have got the side to a respectable position here, with the trail coming down to 363.
Turned through mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Floated outside off, de Silva gets down the track and pushes it to covers.
Dropped on a length around middle and leg, Mendis goes back quickly and works it through backward square leg to rotate strike.
Full on off, driven back to where it came from.
On off, blocked solidly.
Outside off, knocked through mid off for one.
FOUR! Streaky but effective. Tossed up in line of the stumps, Mendis presses forward to defend. The ball takes the inside edge and rolls through to the fine leg fence.
Mendis camps on the back foot and defends it showing the full face of the bat.
Floated around off and middle, kept out with a straight bat.
Bowled on the stumps, defended off the front foot.
On the stumps, swept through square leg for one. The stand moves to 142, trail down to 371.
Bowled on the pads, nudged fine down the leg side for three runs.
Around middle, turned through short leg for one.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Again! Hit straight to mid on from the crease. The fielder again throws it needlessly to the keeper.
Floated around off and middle, pushed to silly mid on. The fielder there has a shy to the keeper, returned by a glare from Mendis.
Outside off, kept out off the back foot.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Kusal takes a run after punching it through covers.
Landed around off, punched towards covers.

Save your head, de Silva! He flicks this off the pads towards square leg. Hesitates a bit before going through with the run. Thankfully for Dhananjaya, he had his eyes on where the ball was. The throw is fired straight at the batter, unintentionally, and he evades it with a slide inside the crease. It the end it looked good but wouldn't have been the case if the batter had been struck.
Flatter on the pads, kept out to the on side.
Taijul Islam back into the attack. He's having a longish chat with his skipper.
Refreshment time!
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! Edged and dropped! Kusal Mendis gets another life! Oh dear, Imrul Kayes is the culprit! Hasan lands it outside off and it goes straight on to open Mendis up. He tries to defend but gets an edge which flies quickly towards the first slip fielder who is late to react. Imrul sticks his left hand out but the ball goes off his fingers and races down to the third man fence. This surely goes down as a chance.

FOUR! Top edge but safe again! Kusal Mendis tries to take on Hasan. Gets down to play the sweep shot but gets it off the top edge. It was in the air for a while but lands safely and Rahim can't stop it from crossing the fence either.
Mendis goes back and flicks it behind square on the leg side. Rahim gets to the ball but couldn't stop them from taking a brace.
Flighted ball around off, eased down to long on for a single.
Tossed up outside off, swept behind square on the leg side for a single.
Mehidy Hasan is back on. Double change from Mahmudullah.
FOUR! Fuller in length and attacking the stumps, driven down the ground past mid on for a boundary. 12 off the over!
Good length delivery on off, blocked off the front foot.

FOUR! Edged but safe! Rahman from around the wicket, bowls an off cutter, it grips off the surface and moves away late. De Silva has a tentative poke at it and it's enough to draw an edge. Luckily for him it evades the dive of the first slip fielder and races away to the fence.
Drives it off the front foot but finds the man at mid off.
FOUR! Edgyyy! Fuller in length and a bit wide outside off, Dhananjaya de Silva goes hard at it. Gets it off the outer half behind point for a boundary.
Good length delivery outside off, poked into the cover region off the back foot.
Tossed up outside off, driven straight to the cover fielder.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.

Overthrows! And that helps Kusal Mendis to get to his fifty, fifth in this format! And my colleague, Suds, who has been very fascinated with numbers these days tells me something about Kusal. He has got to a fifty after 17 international innings. Hmmmm! Ball - A bit short and outside off, punched towards the cover-point fielder. The batsmen are confused as to take the single or not. The fielder there fires a throw at the bowler's end but misses his shy. There is no one backing up either which allows the pair to take four runs.
Flatter delivery on the stumps, Mendis rocks back to pull but mistimes it towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter delivery around middle and leg, clipped past the short leg fielder.
Change of ends for Taijul Islam.
Fuller on off, driven towards the cover fielder.

FOUR! Ahhhhh, that's off the meat again! Relied more on timing this time! Slants it on a length outside off, but offers a bit of width. De Silva presses forward and nails the drive on the up. Splits the gap in the cover region and picks up another boundary to his name. Dhananjaya is oozing in confidence!
Stabs this length ball to the man at point.

FOUR! Effortless! Rahman overcooks it on the stumps, de Silva lunges ahead and presents a straight bat. The ball connects the sweet spot of the bat to beat the dive of the fielder at mid off. Brings up the 100-run stand as well. Sri Lanka on the charge here.
Good length delivery, angling across the batsman, pushed into the cover region.
Fuller in length from over the wicket by going wider of the crease, de Silva looks to turn it away but gets a soft leading edge to the left of the bowler.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on.
This time Mendis flicks the ball which is outside off through mid-wicket. Places it in the gap and takes two more. 11 off the over and Mendis is just 4 short of a half century.
Loopy delivery on off, blocked out into the ground.
FOUR! Exceptional use of the feet! Comes down the track, takes it on the full and whips it through the gap at mid-wicket. Second boundary of the over.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total. Sensible batting!

FOUR! Help yourself delivery! Dhananjaya de Silva brings up his third Test fifty. He scored a ton in his last Test which he played against India and has continued his good run. Sri Lanka were in a bit of trouble at the start but he came in with a lot of intent and look what he has done - bailed his side out in a stunning manner. Played, DDS! Short ball, wide outside off, slapped square of the wicket through point for a blazing boundary.
Flighted delivery around off, blocked nicely.
Floated delivery around middle and off, Kusal Mendis lunges forward and defends it with his bat and pad close together.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Sits deep in the crease and defends it down.
Dances down the track and nudges it past short leg for a single.
Fractionally short and outside off, punched off the back foot to the cover fielder.
Tossed up ball around middle and leg, bunted back to the bowler.
Uses his feet, gets to the pitch of the ball and milks a single towards long off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Steps out of the crease and clips it wide of Tamim at mid on for a single.
Goes back and punches it towards Sunzamul Islam.
Slower and fuller in length outside off, driven towards widish mid off for a single.
Pushed back to the bowler by De Silva.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
DDS drives this down to long off for a single.
A bit too straight and full, flicked through backward square leg for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Slower through the air outside off, dabbed away.

Another run out chance! This is not good between the batters. Earlier, it was Mendis who wanted a run this time it's de Silva. Payback time? Maybe! Around middle and leg, Mendis clips it off the pads. De Silva sets off but Imrul Kayes from first slip gets across to his left and stops it. Mendis sends his partner back and the Bangladesh opener scores a direct hit at the bowler's end but the batsman has made it in. The ball deflects off the timber but they don't run.
De Silva presses forward and drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Lunges forward to a tossed up delivery and blocks.
Hangs back to a flatter ball and keeps it out.
Slightly short and outside off, punched to deep cover for a single.
Loopy ball outside off, defended off the front foot comfortably.
Darted on the pads, flicked away towards mid-wicket for a single.

Mendis is home! Maybe, a better throw was needed. Mendis comes down the track and pushes it towards wide mid off. He sets off as soon as he connects this. De Silva at the other end isn't interested and sends him back. The fielder fires a wide throw to the keeper who has to move a bit to his right and then take the bails off as Kusal drags his bat in. They take it upstairs and replays find Mendis home comfortably.
A mix up but seems all's well in the end. Still the umpire has asked the help of the TV umpire for a run out appeal against Mendis.
Dhananjaya de Silva camps back to a short ball and punches it through cover for a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Goes back and pushes it towards the off side.
Steps out of the crease to a loopy delivery and eases it down to long off for one.
Around middle and leg, nudged through square leg for a single.
Flicked through square leg and will retain strike.
Floated ball around off, blocked.
Lunges forward and drives it towards the mid off fielder for nothing.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Slower again, but the length is short. KM punches it to backward point.
Tosses it up slower through the air, wider outside off, Mendis lets it go unharmed.
Loopy ball around off, blocked off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Drags his length short and it's crunched to deep cover for one.
FOUR! Easily done! Quicker but the line is on the leg stump, Mendis gets inside the line and tickles it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Flatter again, this time a bit outside off, punched off the back foot to mid off for a single.
Flatter ball on the stumps, defended off the back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

SIX! This was asking to be hit and Kusal Mendis says, thank you very much! Gets a half-tracker, Kusal goes deep in the crease and pulls it with aplomb. Where is the ball? Has it bounced or has gone over the fence? A lot of time is taken to make the decision. That's gone the distance.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Flatter delivery outside off, Mendis doesn't play at it.
Sees the flight and decides to go after it by coming down the track. Lofts it over mid-wicket, isn't in control of it but there is no one in the deep. Collects a brace.
Floated delivery outside off, Mendis is happy to keep this one out.
Islam drags his length short, Mendis sits back and slaps it through cover-point. The fielder gives it a good chase to save a run for his side.
Gets behind the line and stonewalls it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Roshen Abeysinghe tells us why Dhananjaya de Silva has been successful till now. He is a very good player of the spin. Uses his feet to great effect, has sweep shots in his armory which is why he is able to negate any turn that is on offer. The others in his team should take a leaf out of this...
Flattish ball on the stumps, tucked in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Very full on middle and leg, worked away wide of mid on for a single.
Flighted delivery outside off, dabbed towards backward point.
Taijul Islam is back into the attack.
Stays back and tucks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Loopy ball on off, kept out off the front foot gently.
Flatter one on the pads, flicked towards the leg side.
Gets nicely forward and buries it into the ground.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up delivery on off, DDS drives it to mid off and gets to the other end very lazily.
Sunzamul Islam will bowl from the other end.
Drops it short and outside off, Mendis cracks it square of the wicket on the off side for a couple of runs.
Shimmies down the track and driven down to long on for a single.
Flattish ball outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover for a single.
Goes back, allows the ball to turn in and then flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Floated ball around off, blocked off the front foot and into the ground.
Starts off with a tossed up ball outside off, Mendis covers his off stump and makes an assured leave.

We're back for the final session. Kusal Mendis and Dhanajaya de Silva will resume their innings. We have 33 overs left in the day. With the way Bangladesh spinners are bowling in tandem, it seems like we should be done in by the scheduled time. Mehidy Hasan to start the proceedings.
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

Bangladesh are still ahead in the game with the heavy first innings total that they have. They were on a roll when they got an early breakthrough but since then have been taken aback. Their spinners are extracting good purchase off the deck and consistency is what they would need, come the final session. There is slow turn so batting isn't that difficult. It's all about patience. Do the Lankans have it in them? Or will Bangladesh run riot? Join us for an exciting final session which will unfold in just a bit...

A good session for Sri Lanka, this! Firstly, they wrapped up the hosts after the lunch break and then have put on a commanding effort to race to their fifty. Dimuth Karunaratne departed for a duck to Mehidy Hasan but Dhananjaya de Silva and his aggressive approach has nullified the openers' loss for the time being. Kusal Mendis looked a bit scratchy at the start (surviving a dropped catch) but looking at his partner attack, he did a sensible job of hanging in out there. The duo has taken the attack to the opposition and their side would bank on the pair to keep it going.
De Silva prods ahead and negotiates the last ball with ease. TEA ON DAY 2!

FOUR! Sliced but the end result matters! Islam bowls it quicker through the air at 89.9 kph, De Silva comes down the track but this time he opts to go inside out. Slices it but has enough behind the shot to clear the man at mid off. Third boundary of the over and it also brings up the 50-run stand between the two.
Lunges ahead and defends it down into the ground.

FOUR! Struck again! This looked even better! The best way to defend is to attack they say and Dhananjaya de Silva is doing exactly that. Tossed up again, the batter skips down the track and belts it down to long off for back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! Boom! Sees the flight, wears his dancing shoes on and kabooms it dead straight over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Loopier ball, landed full around off, blocked out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Advances down the track and milks it down to long on for a single.
FOUR! In the air... safe! Floats it up outside off, dipping in. De Silva gets down and sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
On a flatter trajectory, defended off the back foot back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, wristed towards mid on.

Good effort in the field! Hasan begins this spell with a short ball, serves it wide outside off, it's slapped through cover. Tamim gives it a long hard chase and does extremely well to pull the ball back in play. They take three till then.
Mehidy Hasan is brought back into the attack. He bowled just an over and removed Karunaratne.
Fires it fuller on middle and leg, worked away towards mid on for a single to end the over.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Nicely looped up outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
De Silva dances down the track to defend but wears it on the pads. The ball lobs towards short leg. They put in a stifled appeal but the umpire shakes his head.
Drifting in from around middle and leg, worked away towards mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up ball outside off, driven towards the cover fielder.
Taijul Islam is brought into the attack.
Slower and turning away, pushed off the front foot to point. A maiden for Islam.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Eased down to long off for a single.
A loopy full toss, dipping in, Kusal gets down on one knee to slog it away but drags it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Flighted ball around off, defended into the ground.
Slightly short, slower through the air and served outside off, Mendis stays back to defend but the ball turns away to beat the outside edge.
Back of a length ball on middle and off, De Silva sticks back in defense.
Short of a length delivery on middle, pulled through square leg for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Gets across and flicks it through the leg side for a single.
Fuller and attacking the stumps, De Silva prods forward in defense.
Comes steaming in and angles it away on a length outside off, De Silva covers the sticks and defends it back to Rahman.
Drops it a touch short, De Silva camps back and attempts to pull it away. Mistimes it towards deep mid-wicket and picks up a single.
Floated ball outside off, driven through cover for a single.
Dhananjaya dances down to this tossed up ball, takes it on the full and flicks it through mid-wicket to get off strike.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Flatter one outside off, punched off the back foot to the cover fielder.

Edged but falls short! Islam knows what exactly the pitch is offering. He slows it through the air, at 77.2 kph, lands it outside off and lures the batsman forward. De Silva presses forward to defend but the ball turns a beat, takes the outside edge but falls short of the first slip fielder.
Fuller but the line is too wide outside off to make the batter play at it.
Back of a length ball on middle and off, KM hangs back in defense.
Goes from around the wicket and angles it in from outside off, Mendis has it covered before making leave.
Outside off, Mendis has got nothing to do with that one.
Angling away from a length outside off, Kusal pokes at it and gets beaten comprehensively.
Fuller on middle and leg, worked away wide of mid on for a single.
Beaten! Slower through the air, at 77.4 kph, Mendis leans forward to block but the ball turns away and beats the outside edge by a whisker.
Slower through the air around middle and off, Mendis hangs back in defense.
Drags his length back a touch, it's slapped straight to the man at cover-point.
A bit quicker but it's a bit too full, kept out watchfully.
Little bit of shimmy down the track from De Silva as he works it away through mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted delivery, landing full outside off, pushed towards cover for a single.
In the fifth stump line, the batter is happy to make a leave.
Goes wide of the crease and once angles it on a length outside off, stabbed out comfortably.
Slightly shorter in length, slanting away outside off, shouldered arms to.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, De Silva stays back in defense.
FOUR! Dhananjaya means business! Anticipates a short ball from Rahman, he swivels just a bit and pummels it over mid-wicket to pick up a boundary.
Angles it away on a length outside off, dabbed towards the man at point.
Mendis sees off the last ball with a forward block.
Outside off, driven to covers.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Eased through covers to rotate strike.

Huuugeee appeal, turned down! Bowled flatter outside off, Dhananjaya gets his stride out to block. Gets hit on the front pad and that makes Islam go up in celebration. The umpire, though, negates the same. The hosts think about the review but then decide against it thinking an inside edge to be present. They are right and wrong. Wrong, as there's no bat involved but right, as the impact was well outside off.
Outside off, pushed towards covers.
Outside off, Mendis looks to play it through the off side but fails to get bat to that.

EDGED AND DROPPED! Who is the cuplrit? Mehidy Hasan. Angling away from Kusal on a length, he stays back and looks to open the bat face and hangs his bat out there for the same. The ball goes off the outer half towards the slip cordon. Hasan dives to his left from second slip but the ball hits him on the wrists and goes to ground. Should have taken this at this level. How costly will this be?
FOUR! Off the mark in style. Rahman bowls it short in length, Mendis goes back and plays the pull shot. The ball goes through front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Hurled on a length outside off, defended towards point.
On a length in line of the stumps, blocked to the on side.
Hurled outside off, Mendis shoulders arms to let it be.
Another change. After picking up a wicket, Hasan is taken out of the attack and Mustafizur Rahman is back on.

FOUR! Good cricket. Dhananjaya de Silva picks the length up early on this occasion. This is a half-tracker on middle, he goes back and heaves it over mid-wicket for yet another boundary. 8 runs off this one.
Outside off, pushed to point.

FOUR! This is what has to be done on such a track. Floated up around middle, Dhananjaya slinks down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket. That goes to the fence and the first boundary of the innings is hit.
Flatter on off, blocked from the crease.
De Silva gets down the track and blocks it.
Outside off, pushed towards covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
What an approach! De Silva gets down and plays a slog sweep to this one. The ball goes towards deep mid-wicket for a single to get going.
Around off, defended off the front foot.
Dhananjaya de Silva walks in at the fall of the early wicket.

OUT! Early strike for the hosts! All through yesterday, Sri Lanka were struggling to get a wicket and here are the hosts, they strike off the 15th ball of the innings. Floated outside off, Karunaratne shouldn't be playing away from his body on this track. He does so and pays the price. He gets his front leg out of the way and then hangs his bat out at that tamely. The ball takes the outside edge and goes to the right of Kayes at first slip. He reacts well and takes it nicely. Staying alert helps. You have to credit Mahmudullah's captaincy here. He brought on the off spinner to bowl to the left-hander after just one over from Rahman and it has worked for his side. The Lankan southpaw bags a duck in his first Test of 2018, after having a stellar 2017.
DK lunges forward to bury this onto the ground.
Flatter on the stumps, blocked off the back foot.
Mehidy Hasan to roll his arm now. An immediate change here. A slip and bat-pad in place.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Lovely bowling. Islam seems ounces away from picking up his maiden scalp. This one is tossed up just around off, it spins past the outer edge of the bat.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Around off and middle, defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Bowled in line of the stumps, defended towards mid-wicket.
Beaten straightaway! Floated outside off, Mendis lunges forward to defend but gets beaten by the away turn on this one.
Sunzamul Islam, the newcomer, will share the new ball from the other end. A slip and a short leg in place.
Dimuth stays in the crease and sees it off. A maiden to begin for Bangladesh.
Full on the pads, Karunaratne misses the flick and the ball goes off his pads to the keeper. Das dives and stops it.
Landed around off, met with a straight bat face off the front foot.
Sprayed down the leg side, Karunaratne misses the flick.
Fuller around off, defended off the front foot.
Rahman begins with a full ball on off and middle, pushed defensively back to the bowler.
